inputs.share_count_basis: 2,509,824k weighted-average and diluted shares per the H1 FY2026 interim EPS note (unchanged since FY2023). The only dilutive instrument is 1.085m share options struck at HK$11.094, anti-dilutive at the current price, so basic = diluted. Held FLAT: there is no SBC to charge (awards are cash-settled) and no buyback programme.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report cash-flow statement line 'Share-based payments' (US$2.9m in FY2025, -US$0.4m FY2024, -US$0.5m FY2023) is the fair-value remeasurement of cash-settled restricted/performance units, not equity-settled compensation; the H1 FY2026 interim states the units are expected to be settled in cash. The cost is therefore already a cash expense inside EBITDA and no owner-FCF add-back/deduction applies. SBC treated as zero (SBC-zero market); house and street bases coincide.
inputs.interest_income_source: FY2025 annual report, finance income (note 27): US$8.516m. Stripped because net cash of US$545m is ~4x the owner-FCF base; the cash pile is added back once in the bridge.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows are USD; the HKEX quote is HKD. fx_rate is USD->HKD (multiply a USD per-share value by 7.8476 to get HKD), Yahoo HKD=X at 2026-10-16T08:52Z. HKD is pegged at 7.75-7.85 so the rate is stable; no dual listing exists for a parity check, but the peg band itself bounds any direction error to <1.3% (a reversed rate would give a per-share value ~60x off, which would be obvious). Unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are HKD, comparable to current_price; USD twins are the model's native output.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are USD, so WACC is built from USD inputs: 10-yr UST ~4.2% + ERP 5.0% x beta ~1.2 for a global Tier-1 auto supplier = ~10.2% cost of equity; debt is 2% of capital so WACC rounds to 10.0%. Used for ALL three scenarios: cyclicality, GM concentration and the China-ownership governance overhang are charged in the bear path and the 30% bear weight, not stacked into the discount rate (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. Full lease cash (FY2025: US$14.8m principal + ~US$2.0m interest; H1 FY2026 total lease outflows US$9.4m) is charged inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path at 0.4% of revenue. Lease liabilities (US$29.6m at 2026-06-30) are EXCLUDED from net debt; total_debt is bank borrowings only (51.213 non-current + 0.147 current). D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 285.0 - 14.7 = 270.3, 5.9% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice in the cash-tax line.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge. Flows are consolidated (100%); NCI (book US$53.5m at 2026-06-30, profit share US$10.5m FY2025 / US$4.5m H1 FY2026) is deducted at US$100m, ~10x its earnings share, because book understates a ~US$10m/yr profit stream.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component build) with the non-US/cyclical adaptations -- Nexteer is a cyclical Tier-1 automotive steering/driveline supplier, an operating company, so the routing table sends it to owner-fcf.md plus owner-fcf-adaptations.md (currency, leases, NCI, matching assets, SBC-zero). FY0 is FY2025 (Dec year-end; H1 FY2026 reported 2026-08-12 and used for the balance-sheet anchors and the FY2026 growth/margin read). 10-year horizon because capex is elevated for the APAC footprint build (H1 FY2026 6.8% of revenue vs 5.6% FY2025) and the owner-FCF margin only matures once capex settles to ~6%. EBITDA path is the company's Adjusted EBITDA less ~0.3pp for recurring 'non-recurring' items (FY2025 had US$24.4m of program-cancellation costs incl. US$32.3m impairments; restructuring/ERIP in 2025-26). Working capital: a manufacturer with trade payables roughly matching receivables + inventory, customer deferred revenue (tooling/engineering prepayments) rising; modest net consumption on growth, wc_capture -5%. Terminal cap 12x FCF (cyclical; equals ~3.8x terminal EBITDA in the base case, inside the stock's own historical EV/EBITDA range). Cash tax: FY2025 cash taxes US$68.9m were 37% of pre-special EBIT because US losses are unsheltered while China/Poland/Mexico pay; H1 FY2026 ETR 21.6%; path ramps 30% -> 26% as the US entity returns to taxable profit, held above a blended statutory ~24% for Pillar Two and the 2027-30 expiry of China high-tech certificates. Buyback_cash is zero: the flat share count is simply the absence of issuance, not a funded convention. Price is a regular close, not after-hours.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: H1 FY2026 revenue +3.9% with bookings (US$4.9bn FY2025, US$3.3bn H1 FY2026) running ahead of revenue (US$4.6bn), management targeting growth above global light-vehicle production (which was flat-to-down in H1 FY2026). Sits between the equity 5yr CAGR (2.3%, depressed by dividends and the FY2022-23 margin trough) and the revenue 5yr CAGR (8.6%, flattered by the FY2020 COVID base).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 2.3% vs revenue 5yr CAGR 8.6%: equity has compounded far more slowly than revenue because margins collapsed FY2020-23 (net margin 3.9% -> 0.9%) and the company kept paying dividends; EPS 5yr CAGR is negative for the same reason. The base case therefore leans on the margin-recovery arc continuing, not on equity history.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series = reported FCF - interest income (SBC is zero throughout; awards are cash-settled). FY2020 128.3, FY2022 18.4, FY2025 138.9 (US$m). The 3yr owner-FCF CAGR of 96% is off the FY2022 trough (commodity spike, program launch costs) and is meaningless as a forward rate; the 5yr figure of 1.6% says cash generation has only just regained its FY2020 level despite 51% more revenue, which is the capex-heavy footprint build and the margin trough combined.

base.narrative: FY2026 tracks H1 (+3.9% revenue, 11.3% adj EBITDA margin) with a ~0.3pp owner haircut for recurring program-cancellation/restructuring charges; growth of 3-4% above a flat Western production base from COEM wins and SbW content, fading to 2.5%; margin creeps to 11.3% and stops (APRs cap it); capex steps down from the 6.8% APAC-build peak to ~6% = D&A.

bull.narrative: SbW/EMB by-wire content and COEM share gains lift growth to 5-6% for five years; mix shift to higher-value systems plus the fixed-cost programme carry the adjusted EBITDA margin to 12.5%; capex normalises to 5.8% once the Thailand/India/China plants are filled.

bear.narrative: A North American production downturn in FY2027 (GM is 34% of revenue; NA ~50%) combined with tariff/China-ownership friction costing a GM re-source: revenue falls 8% over two years, the FY2023-style margin trough (9%) returns with fixed-cost deleverage, and the recovery only reaches 10% as APRs and tariff costs are not fully recovered. Cash tax stays at 30% because US losses remain unsheltered.

scenario_narratives.base: Nexteer keeps compounding revenue 3-4% a year against a flat Western light-vehicle market, on the strength of US$4.9bn of FY2025 bookings (52% new/conquest, 34% Chinese OEMs) and the first mass-production Steer-by-Wire launches in 2026. The margin-recovery arc (gross margin 8.8% FY2023 -> 11.4% FY2025; adjusted EBITDA 9.9% -> 10.3% -> 11.3% in H1 FY2026) extends one more step and then stalls at ~11.3%, because annual price-downs to OEMs cap the hardware economics. Capex, elevated at 6.8% of revenue for the Thailand/India/China footprint, settles back to ~6% (= D&A) by FY2030, which is what lifts the owner-FCF margin from ~2% in FY2026 to ~3.5% at maturity. The net cash pile (US$545m, ~38% of market cap) and the US$24m JV and US$16m financial asset are added once in the bridge; NCI and unfunded retirement obligations are deducted once.
scenario_narratives.bull: By-wire content wins the argument: SbW and electro-mechanical braking add content-per-vehicle on Chinese NEV and robotaxi platforms, COEM share keeps rising and is exported to Europe/South America, so revenue grows 5-6% for five years. Mix shift to higher-value systems, software (MotionIQ) attach and the fixed-cost programme carry the adjusted EBITDA margin to 12.5%; capex normalises at 5.8% once the new plants fill. This case needs three independent things to go right (by-wire adoption, COEM share, margin) and is weighted 20%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Customer concentration and the ownership overhang bite together. A North American production downturn in FY2027 (GM 34% of revenue, Stellantis/Ford next) and US restrictions or tariff friction on a China-state-controlled supplier cost a GM platform re-source; revenue falls ~8% over two years and the FY2023-style 9% EBITDA margin trough returns with fixed-cost deleverage. Recovery is slow (2% growth, 10% margin ceiling) because APRs and tariff costs are only partly recovered, and cash tax stays at 30% with US losses unsheltered. Weighted 30% because the customer dependency and the geopolitical exposure are structural, not cyclical.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: a single customer at 34% of revenue, the top five at 76%, a cyclical industry with Western production already negative, and majority Chinese state-linked ownership of a supplier to GM/Ford/Stellantis during strained US-China relations -- all structural. Bull cut from 35% to 20% because it needs by-wire adoption, COEM share gains and a 12.5% margin to land together. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A cash-rich, thin-margin, cyclical Tier-1 supplier valued on consolidated owner FCF with every non-operating item handled exactly once: interest income stripped and cash added back; JV and financial-asset income excluded and the assets added; NCI deducted at earnings value; leases charged in the flows and excluded from debt; SBC zero because awards are cash-settled. Cyclicality, GM concentration and the China-ownership overhang are priced in the bear path and its 30% weight rather than in the discount rate. The terminal is capped at 12x FCF (~3.8x EBITDA), so the value does not depend on the market re-rating a stock that trades at ~1.9x EV/EBITDA.
key_risks_to_valuation: GM is ~34% of revenue and the top five customers 76%; a platform re-source or a North American truck/SUV downturn hits revenue and the fixed-cost base at once (bear case).

Majority AVIC/Pacific Century Motors ownership exposes a supplier to US OEMs to tariff, USMCA-content and CFIUS-style restrictions; this is also why the stock carries a persistent HK discount that a DCF cannot promise will close.
Margin ceiling: contracts carry annual price-downs, raw materials are 65% of revenue, and the FY2023 trough (8.8% gross margin) shows how fast margins compress in a commodity spike.

Capitalised engineering/product development (US$655m) and PP&E (US$1,009m) are exposed to program-cancellation impairments (US$32m in FY2025); the base case haircuts EBITDA ~0.3pp for these but a large cancellation would exceed it.
Cash tax leakage: US losses are unsheltered while China/Poland/Mexico pay; China high-tech tax certificates expire 2027-30 and Pillar Two applies, so the 26% long-run cash rate could prove low.
Balance-sheet anchors are from 2026-06-30; the FY2026 result (due March 2027) will move net cash and the FY2026 driver year.
